title: Molecular Fingerprinting in Cancer Detection
summary:
The development of appropriate diagnostic procedures for cancer using blood samples requires research into the blood of cancer patients and patients suffering from other diseases.

In the study “Molecular Fingerprinting for Cancer Detection” according to the Medical Devices Regulation blood samples from different cohorts are examined using “molecular fingerprinting” (short: MF). The Chair of Laser Physics at LMU under the direction of Prof. Ferenc Krausz has developed this new method. It is based on field-resolved spectroscopy (FRS) of molecular vibrations in blood samples. The evaluation is carried out using modern machine learning approaches.
A total of 38,000 participants are to be included in the study within ten years, divided into the following groups:
1) Patients with certain cancers (lung, prostate, bladder, breast, ovaries, head and neck, liver, colon, pancreas, leukemia),
2) Patients with benign diseases of the same organs as controls,
3) Healthy participants as controls.

A small amount of blood is drawn from all participants during a visit and basic information is collected using a questionnaire (self-reporting). For patients we also document additional medical information (such as the exact diagnosis and the histology) and all information is recorded in a database. Blood sampling from patients takes place in frame of clinical routine and does not affect their treatment.
Some of the cancer patients are also asked to participate in a longitudinal sub-study with additional visits.

The aim of this study is to investigate whether the presence of cancer can be better assessed with this new procedure than with previous procedures.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Informed consent, ≥ 18 years, healthy subject, or one of the eligible benign or malignant diseases.
Exclusion criteria:
Multiple cancers, any cancer therapy within the last two years, no blood draw possible, participant noncompliance
